rituals.goal: Test whether your own name quietly makes its letters feel better.
rituals.mission: Test whether your own name quietly makes its letters feel better.
rituals.rule: Judge the letters themselves, not words they form.
rituals.one_rule: Judge the letters themselves, not words they form.

rituals.safety: Use manageable identity material for one pass. If a single event starts hardening into a global self-judgment, end there and name the behaviour only.

rituals.goal: Climb one social-knowledge ladder without guessing feelings.
rituals.mission: Climb one social-knowledge ladder without guessing feelings.
rituals.play: Take a simple fact such as 'the meeting moved to 3pm.' Mark: I know it; they know it; I know that they know it. Stop at the highest level actually supported.
rituals.twist: Do not fill unsupported levels with assumptions.
rituals.win: Social knowledge becomes layered instead of collapsing into 'everyone knows.'

rituals.safety: Stay with an easily exited imagined audience for one pass. If greater shame or threat develops, end there; go back to observable reality.

rituals.play: In an imagined social scene, distribute ten points among PEOPLE, TASK, and ROOM based on what actually deserves focus.
